prévention et répression du blanchiment de
capitaux, du financement du terrorisme et du
financement de la prolifération des armes de
destruction massive, spécialement en ses
articles 9, 18, 21, 27, 31, 32 et 33;
Revu le Règlement n° 002/FIC/2023 du
26/06/2023 relatif à la lutte contre le
blanchiment de capitaux, le financement du
terrorisme et le financement de la prolifération
des armes de destruction massive;
ÉMET LE RÈGLEMENT SUIVANT:
CHAPITRE PREMIER: DISPOSITIONS
GÉNÉRALES

articles.heading: Purpose of these Regulations These Regulations determine – (a) registration modalities for a reporting
articles.text:
person;
(b) measures applied for customer due
diligence;
(c) modalities for record keeping if a
reporting person suspends or ceases the
activities;
(d) the threshold and requirements relating
to wire transfers, payment or value
transfers;
(e) countermeasures proportionate to the
risks emanating from high-risk
jurisdictions;
(f) modalities and time limits for submission
of a report of suspicious transactions; and
48
(g) the threshold, modalities and time limits
for the reporting of cash transactions or
wire transfers, or value transfers.

articles.heading: Interpretation In these Regulations
articles.text:
(a) “beneficial owner” includes a natural
person who ultimately owns or controls
a customer or the natural person on
whose behalf a transaction is being
conducted. It also includes a natural
person who exercises ultimate effective
control over a legal person or
arrangement;
(b) “beneficiary” means the natural or
legal person who is identified by the
originator as the receiver of the
requested wire transfer, payments or
value transfer in a chain of wire
transfer, payments or value transfers;
49
(c) “beneficiary financial institution”
means the financial institution that
services the account of the beneficiary
or remits cash to the beneficiary which
is the end point in the payment chain;
(d) “Centre” means the national authority
in charge of financial intelligence;
(e) “cross-border wire transfer, payment
or value transfer” means any wire
transfer, payment or value transfer
where the ordering financial institution
and beneficiary financial institution are
located in different countries. This term
also refers to any chain of wire transfer,
payments or value transfers in which at
least one of the financial institutions
involved is located in a different
country;
(f) “domestic wire transfer, payment or
value transfer” means a wire transfer,
payment or value transfer where the
50
ordering financial institution and
beneficiary financial institution are
located in the same country. This term
refers to a chain of wire transfer,
payments or value transfers that takes
place entirely within the borders of a
single country, even though the system
used to transfer the payment message
may be located in another country;
(g) “intermediary financial institution”
means a financial institution in payment
chain that receives and transmits a wire
transfer, payment or value transfer on
behalf of the ordering financial
institution and the beneficiary financial
institution or another intermediary
financial institution;
(h) “legal arrangement” means a trust
created by the settlor in the form of a
written deed or other similar legal
arrangements;
51
(i) “occasional customer” means a
customer who occurs or appears at
irregular or infrequent basis;
(j) “ordering financial institution,”
means a financial institution that
receives the instructions from the
originator for the transfer of the funds
to the beneficiary. The institution is the
start point of payment chain;
(k) “originator” means an account holder
who requests the wire transfer,
payment or value transfer from that
account, or if there is no account, the
natural or legal person that places the
order with the ordering financial
institution to perform the wire transfer,
payment or value transfer;
(l) “politically exposed person”
includes –
52
(i) a foreign politically exposed
person, who is or has been
entrusted with prominent public
functions by a foreign country,
such as head of State or of
Government, senior politician,
senior government, judicial or
military official, senior executive
of State-owned corporation,
important political party official;
(ii) a domestic political exposed
person, who is or has been
entrusted domestically with
prominent public functions, such
head of State or of Government,
senior politician, senior
government, judicial or military
official, senior executive of Stateowned corporation, important
political party official;
(iii)a person who is or has been
entrusted with a prominent
function by an international
organisation and who is a member
53
of senior management, such as
director, deputy director and
member of the board or equivalent
functions; and
(iv)family members of a politically
exposed person provided for in
Subparagraphs (n)(i), (ii), and (ii)
as well as their close associates
persons;
(m) “supervisory authority” means the
authority that regulates, supervises,
controls and monitors the functioning
of reporting persons;
(n) “suspicious transaction or activity”
means a transaction or attempted
transaction, activity or attempted
activity where a reporting person has
suspicions or reasonable grounds to
suspect that is related to money
laundering, terrorist financing and
financing of proliferation of weapons
of mass destruction;
(o) “wire transfer, payment or value
transfer” means a transaction carried
54
out on behalf of an originator through
an ordering financial institution by
electronic means with a view of
availing amount of funds to a
beneficiary at a beneficiary financial
institution, irrespective of whether the
originator and the beneficiary are the
same, including cash withdrawals.
CHAPTER II: RISK MANAGEMENT AND
REGISTRATION MODALITIES

articles.heading: Registration of a reporting person
Time for registration of a reporting person (1) A new reporting person registers with the Centre within 30 days after getting the
articles.text:
certificate of incorporation.
55
(2) A reporting person notifies the Centre, in
writing, of a change to the particulars
furnished during the registration within
seven working days from the dater the
change took place.

articles.heading: Risk-based approach and institutional obligations A reporting person – (a) develops and applies a risk-based approach
articles.text:
in implementing anti-money laundering,
countering the financing of terrorism and
countering proliferation financing
measures, ensuring that the intensity of
measures is proportionate to the risks
identified;
(b) conducts and documents an institutional
risk assessment on money laundering,
terrorist financing and the financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction, at least once a year and
whenever there is a significant change in
56
their business, customer profile, or
services offered; and
(c) ensures their risk assessment and internal
controls are informed by the national risk
assessment and a relevant sectoral risk
assessment.

articles.heading: Designation of a compliance officer (1) A reporting person designates a compliance officer who is in charge of
articles.text:
ensuring compliance with requirements
related to anti-money laundering,
terrorist financing, and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction.
(2) The compliance officer is at managerial
level with sufficient authority, seniority,
and resources to perform the duties
effectively and independently.
57
(3) The compliance officer has direct and
unfettered access to the Board of
Directors or a relevant committee
thereof, and reports compliance status
independently in the meetings of Board
of Directors.
(4) A reporting person informs the Centre of
the designated compliance officer within
three working days following the
appointment.
(5) Whenever there is a change in relation to
the compliance officer, the reporting
person notifies the Centre within 24
hours from the occurrence of that change.
CHAPTER III: MEASURES APPLIED FOR
CUSTOMER DUE DILIGENCE

articles.heading: Basic customer due diligence (1) A reporting person applies basic 58 customer due diligence measures before
articles.text:
entering into a business relationship, in
the framework of combating money
laundering and associated predicate
offences, combating terrorist financing
and financing of proliferation of weapons
of mass destruction.
(2) The basic customer due diligence
includes –
(a) identification and verification of the
identity of the customer and
beneficial ownership; and
(b) understanding and, as appropriate,
obtaining information on the purpose
and intended nature of the business
relationships.

articles.heading: Simplified customer due diligence measures (1) Simplified customer due diligence measures for combating money
articles.text:
laundering, terrorist financing or
financing of proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction includes –
59
(a) to verify the identity of the customer
and the beneficial owner after the
establishment of the business
relationship;
(b) to reduce the frequency of customer
identification updates;
(c) to reduce the degree of ongoing
monitoring and scrutinising
transactions based on a reasonable
monetary threshold as specified by
the Centre; and
(d) not to collect specific information or
carry out specific measures to
understand the purpose and intended
nature of the business relationship
but inferring the purpose and nature
from the type of transactions or
business relationship established.
(2) Simplified customer due diligence
measures are not acceptable whenever
there is a suspicion of money laundering,
terrorist financing or financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction.
60

articles.heading: Enhanced customer due diligence measures The enhanced customer due diligence measures for combating money laundering, terrorist
articles.text:
financing or financing of proliferation of
weapons of mass destruction include –
(a) to obtain additional information on the
customer including occupation, volume
of assets, information available through
public databases and internet, and to
update regularly identification data of
customer and beneficial owner;
(b) to obtain additional information on the
intended nature of the business
relationship;
(c) to obtain information on the source of
funds or wealth of the customer;
(d) to obtain information on the reasons for
intended or performed transaction;
61
(e) to obtain approval of senior management
to commence or continue the business
relationship;
(f) to conduct enhanced monitoring of the
business relationship, by increasing the
number and timing of controls applied
and selecting patterns of transactions that
need further examination; and
(g) to require the first payment to be carried
out through an account in the customer’s
name with a bank subject to similar
customer due diligence standards.

articles.heading: Customer due diligence to politically exposed persons (1) A reporting person develops and implements appropriate risk
articles.text:
management systems to determine if a
customer or beneficial owner is a
politically exposed person.
(2) A foreign politically exposed person is
always treated as a high-risk customer.
62
(3) For a customer or beneficial owner who
is a domestic or international
organisation’s politically exposed
person, the reporting person has to
identify the risk associated with this
customer or the beneficial owner.
(4) If a domestic or international
organisation’s politically exposed person
is determined to be high-risk customer,
the reporting person applies enhanced
measures.

articles.heading: Basic requirements for account opening (1) The basic requirements for account opening include –
articles.text:
(a) the customer and beneficial
ownership identification and the
identity number;
(b) identification of signatories;
(c) the complete professional and
personal address of the customer;
63
(d) the legal form, status and structure of
the legal person or legal arrangement;
(e) the country of establishment of the
legal person or of the legal
arrangement;
(f) a proof of incorporation and address
of the registered office of an activity
of a legal person or legal arrangement;
(g) the nature and purpose of an activity
of the customer; and
(h) the expected use of the account.
(2) Subject to the requirements provided for
in Paragraph (1), a reporting person may
put in place other requirements for
opening an account.
64

articles.heading: Obligation of a reporting person towards a person acting on behalf of a customer A reporting person verifies that a person acting
articles.text:
on behalf of a customer is authorised to do so.
The reporting person identifies and verifies the
identity of the person acting on behalf of the
customer.

articles.heading: Non-face-to-face customer identification and verification A reporting person – (a) identifies and verifies the identification
articles.text:
of a non-face-to-face customer in the
same manner with the procedures
applicable to the face-to-face customer
identification and verification; and
(b) puts in place measures for avoiding
fraud by single or multiple false
applications.

articles.heading: Special monitoring of business relationship and certain transactions A reporting person – 65
articles.text:
(a) pays special attention to complex and
unusual forms of transactions, especially
large transactions which have no
apparent or lawful economic purpose,
examines the background, the source and
purpose of such transactions, establishes
findings in writing and transmits the
report to the Centre; and
(b) pays special attention to business
relationship and transaction between its
customer and person residing in a
country with high risk of money
laundering, terrorist financing and
financing of proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction.

articles.heading: Customer due diligence measures for specific transactions A reporting person applies customer due
articles.text:
diligence measures, if the customer –
(a) carries out an occasional transaction
with an amount equal to or above FRW
66
10,000,000 or its equivalent in foreign
currency, whether conducted as a single
transaction or several transactions that
appear to be linked;
(b) carries out an occasional transaction that
is a domestic or cross-border wire
transfer, payment or value transfer equal
to or above FRW 1,000,000 or its
equivalent in foreign currency, whether
conducted as a single transaction or
several transactions that appear to be
linked;
(c) carries out a financial transaction of
casino equal to or above FRW 3,000,000
or its equivalent in foreign currency,
whether conducted as a single transaction
or several transactions that appear to be
linked;
(d) is involved in a transaction for a
customer concerning the buying and
selling of a real estate. The due diligence
measures apply to both seller and buyer
of the real estate;
67
(e) who deals in precious metals or precious
stones, carries out a cash transaction
equal to or above FRW 15,000,000 or its
equivalent in foreign currency, whether
conducted as a single transaction or
several transactions that appear to be
linked; or
(f) for a trust and company service provider,
prepares or carries out a transaction
concerning the following activities:
(i) to act as a formation and
incorporation agent of a legal person;
(ii) to act as or arrange for another person
to act as a director or secretary of a
company, a partner of a partnership,
or a similar position in relation to
other legal persons;
68
(iii)to provide a registered office,
business address or accommodation,
correspondence or administrative
address for a company, a partnership
or any other legal person or
arrangement;
(iv)to act as or arrange for another person
to act as a trustee of an express trust
or performing the equivalent function
for another form of a legal
arrangement;
(v) to act as or arrange for another person
to act as a nominee shareholder for
another person.

articles.heading: Due diligence measures to a potential customer (1) A reporting person applies due diligence
articles.text:
measures to a potential customer.
(2) In case the reporting person believes that
performing customer due diligence may
tip-off the potential customer, it is
69
permitted not to perform customer due
diligence and to submit a report to the
Centre.

articles.heading: Due diligence on existing customer (1) A reporting person, on the basis of materiality of the risk, applies existing
articles.text:
customer due diligence on the existing
business relationship at appropriate
times, taking into account when due
diligence measures have previously been
undertaken and the adequacy and
accuracy of data obtained.
(2) A reporting person terminates the
business relationship with an existing
customer if the reporting person has
doubts about the veracity of previously
obtained customer identification data,
and if the existing customer holds an
anonymous account or an account in
fictitious names and immediately
submits a report on the suspicious
transaction.
70

articles.heading: Due diligence on a customer from a high-risk country A reporting person conducts enhanced customer
articles.text:
due diligence for business relationship and
transaction with a customer from a country
identified as high risk and not efficiently
complying with international standards or
having ongoing or substantial risk of money
laundering, terrorist financing and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

articles.heading: Counter measures applied to a high-risk country A reporting person undertakes counter-measures
articles.text:
against a high-risk country, including –
(a) to introduce enhanced reporting
mechanisms;
(b) not to establish a subsidiary, branch or
representative office from that country;
(c) to limit business relationship with that
country or a person in that country;
71
(d) not to rely on information from third
party located in that country to conduct
the customer due diligence;
(e) to review and amend, or if necessary,
terminate correspondent relationships
with financial institution from that
country;
(f) to conduct supervisory examination or
external audit for a branch and subsidiary
of a reporting person based in that
country;
(g) to apply external audit requirements for
financial group with respect to one of its
branches or subsidiaries located in that
country; and
(h) other measures that may have a similar
effect in mitigating risks.

articles.heading: Correspondent banking In relation to cross-border correspondent banking and other similar relationships, a
articles.text:
72
financial institution applies customer due
diligence measures provided for by the law. The
other similar relationships include those
established for securities transactions or funds
transfers, whether for the cross-border financial
institution as principal or for its customers.
CHAPTER IV: REQUIREMENTS
RELATING TO WIRE TRANSFER,
PAYMENT OR VALUE TRANSFER

articles.heading: Information on the payment chain (1) A financial institution collects required and accurate originator information, and
articles.text:
requires beneficiary information on a
wire transfer, payment and value transfer
and related messages, and ensures that
the information remains with the wire
transfer, payment and value transfer or
related message throughout the payment
chain.
73
(2) An ordering financial institution and
intermediary financial institution in the
payment chain ensure that required
originator information and beneficiary
information that accompany a wire transfer,
payment or value transfer, or related
message is transmitted with the transfer.
(3) A financial institution identifies which
other financial institution is servicing the
account of the originator and beneficiary,
and in which countries these institutions are
located.

articles.heading: De minimis threshold De minimis threshold for both domestic and cross-border wire transfers, payments or value
articles.text:
transfers other than cash withdrawals is FRW
1,000,000 or its equivalent in other currency.
74

articles.heading: Cross-border wire transfer, payment, or value transfer below de minimis threshold (1) For cross-border wire transfer, payment
articles.text:
or value transfer below de minimis
threshold, a financial institution records
the following related information:
(a) the name of the originator and
beneficiary;
(b) the account number of the originator
and beneficiary, where such an
account is used to process the
transaction, if there is no account, a
unique transaction reference
number. In cases where the funds are
drawn from a financial institution
other than the ordering financial
institution, the account number, and
the name of financial institution
from where the funds are drawn are
included.
75
(2) The required information provided for in
Paragraph (1) is not subject to
verification for accuracy, unless there is
a suspicion of money laundering,
terrorist financing or financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction in which case, the reporting
person verifies the information
pertaining to its customer.

articles.heading: Cross-border wire transfer, payment, or value transfer above de minimis threshold For the cross-border wire transfer, payment, or
articles.text:
value transfer above de minimis threshold, a
financial institution records the following related
information:
(a) the name of the originator and
beneficiary;
(b) the account number of the originator and
beneficiary where such an account is
used to process the transaction; if there is
no account, a unique transaction
reference number;
76
(c) the address of the originator and the
country and town name or the nearest
alternative of the beneficiary. In the
absence of standardised postal address
information for originator, the name of
the country and town or the nearest
alternative;
(d) the date of birth of the originator if the
originator is a natural person. If the full
information of the date of the birth is not
available, the year of the birth is
required;
(e) if the originator or beneficiary is a legal
person, the following information are
recorded, if any:
(i) the connected business identifier
code;
(ii) the legal entity identifier; or
(iii)the unique official identifier of the
originator or beneficiary.
77

articles.heading: Domestic wire transfer, payment, or value transfer below de minimis threshold (1) For domestic wire transfer, payment or
articles.text:
value transfer below de minimis
threshold, a financial institution records
the following related information:
(a) the name of the originator; and
(b) the account number of the originator
or unique transaction reference
number which permits the
transaction to be traced back to the
originator or the beneficiary.
(2) The required information provided for in
Paragraph (1) is not subject to
verification for accuracy, unless there are
a suspicion of money laundering,
terrorist financing and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction in which case, the financial
institution verifies the information
pertaining to its customer.
78

articles.heading: Domestic wire transfer, payment, or value transfer above the de minimis threshold (1) For domestic wire transfer, payment, or
articles.text:
value transfer above the de minimis
threshold, a financial institution records
the originator information as provided
for in Article 25, unless this information
is available to the beneficiary financial
institution and appropriate authorities by
other means. In this case, the ordering
financial institution includes the account
number or unique transaction reference
number, provided that this number or
identifier permit the transaction to be
traced back to the originator or
beneficiary.
(2) The information provided for in
Paragraph (1) are recorded and made
available by the ordering financial
institution within three working days of
receiving the request either from the
beneficiary or intermediary financial
79
institution or from appropriate competent
authorities.

articles.heading: Exceptions and differentiated requirements (1) No information is required for transfers and settlements carried out between
articles.text:
financial institutions, if both the
originator and beneficiary are financial
institutions operating on their own
behalf.
(2) If a net settlement results from wire
transfer, payment or value transfer
transactions carried out on behalf of
customers, information about the
underlying transactions is not required to
accompany the net settlement. However,
the requirements of Articles 23, 24, 25
and 26 apply to the underlying
transactions themselves.
(3) If several individual cross-border wire
transfers, payments or value transfers
80
from a single originator are bundled in a
batch file for transmission to
beneficiaries they are exempted from the
requirements of Articles 23 and 24, in
respect of originator information,
provided that they record the originator’s
account number or unique transaction
reference number as provided in Article
23 (b) and the batch file contains required
and accurate originator information, and
full beneficiary information, that is fully
traceable within the beneficiary country.
(4) With respect to transfers that flow from a
transaction carried out using a credit,
debit or prepaid card for the purchase of
goods or services, the card number has to
be recorded on all transfers resulting
from the transaction. The name and
location of the card issuing and merchant
acquiring financial institutions must be
made available to other financial
institutions in the payment chain and,
through them, to the competent
81
authorities upon request.
(5) If a credit, debit or prepaid card is used to
effect other types of payment or value
transfer, the transaction is subject to the
provisions of Articles 23, 24, 25 and 26.
(6) A financial institution records a used
account number or card number
information for domestic cash
withdrawals.
(7) In order to use a credit, debit or prepaid
card through a different financial
institution for cross-border cash
withdrawals, the following requirements
apply:
(a) the card number which accompanies
cash withdrawal;
82
(b) the name of the cardholder has to be
sent to the acquiring financial
institution upon request, within three
working days from the date of receipt
of the request.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of an ordering financial institution (1) An ordering financial institution has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to ensure that cross-border wire
transfer, payment or value transfer
above the de minimis threshold
contains required and accurate
originator information, and required
beneficiary information;
(b) to ensure that cross-border wire
transfer, payment or value transfer
below the de minimis threshold
contains the name of the originator
and the beneficiary and an account
number for each, or a unique
transaction reference number;
83
(c) to maintain originator and
beneficiary information collected in
accordance with record keeping
requirements.
(2) The ordering financial institution does
not execute the wire transfer, payment or
value transfer if it does not comply with
the requirements provided for in
Paragraph (1).

articles.heading: Responsibilities of an intermediary financial institution (1) For a cross-border wire transfer, payment
articles.text:
or value transfer, a financial institution
acting as an intermediary in the
processing of such chains of transfers
must ensure that the originator and
beneficiary information that
accompanies a wire transfer, payment or
value transfer is retained with it.
(2) If technical limitations prevent the
required information accompanying a
84
cross-border wire transfer, payment or
value transfer from remaining with a
related domestic wire transfer, payment
or value transfer, records are kept, for at
least ten years, by the receiving
intermediary financial institution of the
information received from the ordering
financial institution or another
intermediary financial institution.
(3) An intermediary financial institution
takes reasonable measures to identify
cross-border wire transfers, payments or
value transfers that lack required
information.
(4) An intermediary financial institution has
effective risk-based policies and
procedures for determining –
(a) when to execute, reject, or suspend a
wire transfer, payment or value
transfer lacking required originator
or required beneficiary information;
85
and
(b) the appropriate follow-up actions.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of a beneficiary financial institution A beneficiary financial institution has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to take reasonable measures to identify
cross-border wire transfers, payments or
value transfers that lack required
originator or beneficiary information.
These measures may include post-event
monitoring or real-time monitoring
where feasible;
(b) for cross-border wire transfers, payments
or value transfers above the de minimis
threshold, to verify the identity of the
beneficiary, if the identity has not been
previously verified, and maintains this
information in accordance with record
keeping requirements. The information
86
received on the intended beneficiary has
to be useful in the monitoring of
beneficiary financial institution with the
objective of detecting misdirected
payments due to possible money
laundering, fraud, or error;
(c) to take measures to mitigate the risk of
transfers being made to an unintended
beneficiary. Such measures include at
least one of the following:
(i) for each transaction, checking the
extent to which the name and account
number of the beneficiary in the
payment message aligns with the
information held by the beneficiary
financial institution;
(ii) to conduct holistic ongoing
monitoring to identify anomalous
accounts, transactions, and activity,
including misaligned beneficiary
information, following a risk-based
approach;
87
(iii)if the beneficiary and ordering
financial institutions both participate
in a prevalidation mechanism such as
confirmation and verification of
payee to check, for each transaction,
that the name and account number of
the beneficiary in the payment
message aligns with the information
held by the beneficiary financial
institution, then this pre-validation
may be used in place of what is
provided for in Subsubparagraphs (i)
or (ii);
(d) to have effective risk-based policies and
procedures for determining –
(i) when to execute, reject, or suspend a
wire transfer, payment or value
transfer lacking required originator
or required beneficiary information
or when they identify potentially
misdirected payments in the
implementation of the requirements
under Subparagraphs (b) and (c); and
88
(ii) the appropriate follow-up actions;
(e) to consider as suspicious a wire transfer,
payment or value transfer or related
transaction that lacks the required
originator information or beneficiary
information and report it to the Centre.

articles.heading: Money or value transfer service provider (1) A money or value transfer service provider complies with the requirements
articles.text:
provided for by these Regulations in the
countries in which the money or value
transfer service provider operates,
directly or through the agents.
(2) A money or value transfer service
provider who controls, or is part of a
money or value transfer service network
controlling both the ordering and the
beneficiary side of a payment or value
89
transfer by –
(a) taking into account the information
from both the ordering and
beneficiary sides in order to
determine whether a suspicious
transaction report has to be filed; and
(b) filing a suspicious transaction report
in a country affected by the
suspicious wire transfers, payments
or value transfers, and making
relevant transaction information
available to the Centre.
CHAPTER V: PREVENTIVE
MECHANISMS

articles.heading: Internal mechanisms and procedures A reporting person establishes internal mechanisms and procedures to communicate to
articles.text:
its employees the internal policies and
procedures in place against money laundering,
terrorist financing and financing of proliferation
of weapons of mass destruction. It has also to
establish a monitoring framework to ensure
90
effective implementation of those policies.

articles.heading: Independent audit (1) A reporting person has an independent audit function to evaluate the following
articles.text:
(a) compliance with policies,
procedures and controls to combat
money laundering, terrorist
financing and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction and to assess whether
current measures are in line with the
latest developments and changes;
(b) the adequacy and effectiveness of the
compliance programme;
(c) reliability, integrity and timeliness of
the internal and regulatory reporting
and management of information
systems.
(2) The reporting person ensures that
independent audit is carried out at
91
institutional level at least once a year and
whenever considered necessary.

articles.heading: Capacity building and awareness programmes (1) A reporting person conducts regular training and awareness programmes to
articles.text:
the staff on practices and measures with
regard to combating money laundering,
terrorist financing and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass
destruction.
(2) The capacity building activities
organised for the staff are in line with
their responsibilities in detecting money
laundering, terrorist financing activities
and financing of proliferation of weapons
of mass destruction and at the level of the
risks of money laundering, terrorist
financing and financing of proliferation
of weapons of mass destruction faced by
the reporting person.
92

articles.heading: Monitoring of foreign branches, subsidiaries and offices (1) A reporting person monitors the foreign
articles.text:
branches, subsidiaries or offices to
ensure that they apply anti-money
laundering, terrorist financing and
financing of proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction measures in accordance
with the home country requirements.
(2) If the country in which foreign branches,
subsidiaries or offices operate does not
permit the proper implementation of the
measures provided for in Paragraph (1),
financial groups and other reporting
persons apply additional measures to
manage the money laundering, terrorist
financing and financing proliferation of
weapons of mass destruction risks.
(3) If the additional measures provided for in
Paragraph (2) are not sufficient, the
supervisory authority in the home
country considers additional supervisory
93
actions, including placing additional
controls on the financial group and,
where necessary, requesting the financial
group to close down its operations in the
host country.

articles.heading: Implementation of targeted financial sanctions A reporting person complies with the relevant
articles.text:
legislations and related guidelines on targeted
financial sanctions and also ensures their
implementation within the timeline set by the
Centre in order to comply with 24 hours which
start from the time of designation.

articles.heading: Supervisory framework The supervisory authority develops and implements risk based supervisory framework to
articles.text:
ensure that reporting persons comply with the
requirements for combating money laundering,
counter terrorist financing and financing of
proliferation of weapons of mass destruction,
including inspections, outreach programmes and
other relevant activities for the reporting persons
under its supervision.
94

articles.heading: Forum The Centre establishes the forum for competent authorities for effective compliance with the
articles.text:
requirements of combating money laundering,
terrorist financing and financing of proliferation
of weapons of mass destruction and for feedback
provision.
CHAPTER VI: MODALITIES AND TIME
LIMIT FOR REPORTING A SUSPICIOUS
TRANSACTION OR ACTIVITY

articles.heading: Modalities of reporting a suspicious transaction or activity (1) A reporting person reports to the Centre
articles.text:
when the reporting person suspects or has
reasonable grounds to suspect that fund
or other asset are the proceeds of a crime,
are related or linked to money
laundering, to terrorist financing, or
financing the proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction, regardless of the
amount involved.
95
(2) A reporting person reports to the Centre
a suspicious transaction or activity using
the template established by the Centre.
(3) The reporting person submits a
suspicious transaction or activity report
to the Centre within 24 hours from its
occurrence. The report is submitted
electronically or in any other channel as
the Centre may determine.
(4) The Centre provides guidance from time
to time in order to assist the reporting
person to comply with the provisions of
these Regulations.

articles.heading: Indicators and technics for identification of suspicious transaction or activity The Centre provides indicators and technics that
articles.text:
serve as a guidance in the identification of a
suspicious transaction or activity.
96
CHAPTER VII: THRESHOLD,
MODALITIES AND TIME LIMIT FOR
REPORTING A TRANSACTION OR
VALUE TRANSFER

articles.heading: Threshold of a transaction or value transfer (1) A reporting person submits to the Centre a report of a cash transaction or value
articles.text:
transfer involving the following
thresholds:
(a) an amount equal to or above FRW
10,000,000 or its equivalent in
foreign currency for an occasional
customer, except if the sender and
recipient are banks or other financial
institutions;
(b) an amount equal to or above FRW
3,000,000 or its equivalent in foreign
currency if it is made in a casino;
(c) an amount equal to or above FRW
15,000,000 or its equivalent in
97
foreign currency if it is done by a
dealer in precious metals and
precious stones.
(2) The amount equal to or above FRW
1,000,000 or its equivalent in foreign
currency, if the transaction or transfer
provided for in Paragraph (1) involves
wire transfer.
(3) The provisions of Paragraph (1) apply to
a transaction or transfer whether
conducted as a single or several
transactions or transfers that appear to be
linked, the total of which exceeds the
threshold.

articles.heading: Modalities and time limit for reporting a transaction or value transfer A reporting person reports to the Centre a cash
articles.text:
transaction, wire transfer or value transfer using
a template provided by the Centre within two
working days from the date of the transaction or
transfer.
98
CHAPTER VIII: MISCELLANEOUS AND
FINAL PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Modalities for record keeping (1) For a transaction, a reporting person maintains necessary records on
articles.text:
transactions both domestic and
international for at least ten years from
the date of completion of the transaction.
(2) For records obtained through customer
due diligence measures, account files and
business correspondences, and results of
an analysis undertaken, a reporting
person maintains them at least ten years
from the date of termination of the
business relationship or after the date of
the occasional transaction.
(3) If a reporting person suspends its
activities or ceases to exist, it submits to
the supervisory authority, within 30 days
from the date of the suspension or
99
cessation of activities, all records kept for
compliance with the requirements of the
prevention and combating of money
laundering, terrorist financing and
financing of proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction.
(4) If a non-profit organisation, suspends its
activities or ceases to exist, it submits to
the authority in charge of regulating,
supervising or monitoring non-profit
organisations, within 30 days from the
date of the suspension or cessation of
activities, all records kept for compliance
with the requirements relating to the
prevention and combating of money
laundering, terrorist financing or and
financing of proliferation of weapons of
mass destruction.
(5) The supervisory authority and the
authority in charge of regulating,
supervising or monitoring non-profit
organisations maintain those records for
compliance with the requirements
relating to the prevention and combating
100
of money laundering, terrorist financing
and financing of proliferation of weapons
of mass destruction received for at least
ten years from the date of their receipt.

articles.heading: Annual compliance report (1) A reporting person submits an annual compliance report indicating the
articles.text:
activities performed in implementing the
anti-money laundering, counter terrorism
financing and financing proliferation of
weapons of mass destruction program.
(2) The report provided for in Paragraph (2)
is submitted to the supervisory authority
with a copy to the Centre using the
template established and within the
indicated time.

repealed.
